our_title: CMake libScotch lacks five Makefile-built sources, so SCOTCH_contextBindMesh and three Fortran wrappers are missing
ran: cmake 4.4.4 (uv cache wheel) build of base-combined, CI flags (-DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=ON): nm -D cm/base32/lib/libscotch.so | grep -E ' T (SCOTCH_contextBindMesh|SCOTCHFCONTEXTBINDMESH|scotchfgraphinducelist_|scotchfgraphinducepart_|scotchfnumsizeof_|_SCOTCHhgraphDump)$' -> nothing; Makefile build (INFRA/asan/lib/libscotch.so) has all six. Patched build (cm/patched32): all six present. Text check: sh ci/check_sources.sh src-base/src -> '< hgraph_dump.c < library_context_mesh.c < library_context_mesh_f.c < library_graph_induce_f.c < library_memory_f.c' (+ '> common_error.c', '> symbol_fax.c', see extra.json), rc=1; on HEAD rc=0. Full details: repro/BLD-01/README.
severity_note: Same as the review: a public routine declared in scotch.h (SCOTCH_contextBindMesh) and documented Fortran wrappers cannot be linked from a CMake-built library, which is what distributions and CI use.
evidence:
src/libscotch/CMakeLists.txt:272-273 'hgraph_check.c
  hgraph_induce.c' (no hgraph_dump.c); :359-362 'library_context.c / library_context_graph.c / library_context_graph_f.c / library_context_f.c' (no library_context_mesh*.c); :381-382 'library_graph_f.c
  library_graph_io_chac.c' (no library_graph_induce_f.c); :404-405 'library_memory.c
  library_mesh.c' (no library_memory_f.c). Makefile LIBSCOTCHDEPS lists hgraph_dump, library_context_mesh, library_context_mesh_f, library_graph_induce_f, library_memory_f. Also :204/:206 'bgraph_cost.c' listed twice and :248 'library_graph_induce.c' misplaced between graph_ielo.c and graph_induce.c.
upstream_change: none: file untouched between v7.0.16 and v7.0.17 (only CMakeLists.txt's version mark, 6ad2737, and ci/test_cmake.sh, ad24b21, changed)
review_accuracy: Accurate on the five files and the consequence. Imprecise on which 'memory' wrapper is lost: library_memory_f.c provides scotchfnumsizeof (SCOTCH_numSizeof), not the memory statistics wrappers (scotchfmemcur/scotchfmemmax live in library_common_f.c, which CMake builds). hgraph_dump.c is an internal debugging helper with no public caller, so its absence only matters for consistency.
first_pass_critique: Status and location right, but the nm evidence is wrong: it cites 'scotchfmemcur' as the symbol of library_memory_f.c, whereas that file defines scotchfnumsizeof (the CMake build has scotchfmemcur from library_common_f.c). It did not run cmake (a working cmake wheel was in the uv cache). It missed that the same list also carries a dead file (common_error.c) that leaks un-prefixed symbols, and the libesmumps mismatch (symbol_fax.c), both found by the very CI check it proposed. Its 'single-source' option 3 is dismissed as 'unlikely to be accepted' without trying it; a working configure-time version exists (alt c).

fix_options.label: a: add the files to SCOTCH_C_SOURCES (+ tidy the list)
fix_options.summary: Add the five .c files and hgraph_dump.h at their alphabetical place, drop the duplicate bgraph_cost.c, move library_graph_induce.c to its place; separate commits remove the dead common_error.c and the standalone symbol_fax.c; a checker script and the Makefile rule typos are separate commits.
fix_options.tested: patched32/patched64 CMake builds: 0 new warnings, nm shows the six symbols, ctest 181/181 (both); suffixed, no-esmumps and static builds also pass; ci/check_sources.sh rc=0 on HEAD.
fix_options.tradeoffs: None: the list simply becomes what the Makefile builds. Exported symbol set of the CMake libscotch gains 6 and loses 3 (errorPrint/errorPrintW/errorProg, patch 0002).
fix_options.maintainer_fit: This is the maintainers' own convention (every file hand-listed, e.g. 5efb923 in the combined series adds library_dgraph_grow_f.c to both Makefile and CMakeLists.txt). Minimal and mechanical.

fix_options.label: b: CI guard only
fix_options.summary: Ship ci/check_sources.sh (diff of Makefile object lists vs CMake source lists for the five libraries) and run it in CI, without fixing the lists.
fix_options.tested: Run on v7.0.17, base-combined (reports the 7 differences, rc=1) and on HEAD (rc=0); see repro/BLD-01/README.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Alone it fails CI without fixing anything; it is the complement of (a), not a replacement. Needs the one-line job described in SUMMARY.md (G30 owns ci/build_cmake.sh / .gitlab-ci.yml).
fix_options.maintainer_fit: He would take it together with (a): CI scripts in ci/ are small POSIX shell scripts like this one. Not as the only fix.

fix_options.label: c: CMake reads the source list from the Makefile
fix_options.summary: Replace set(SCOTCH_C_SOURCES ...) by a function that parses LIBSCOTCHDEPS of src/libscotch/Makefile at configure time (file(READ), continuation lines joined, MATCHALL on xxx$(OBJ)).
fix_options.tested: configure-tested only: cmake -S altwork2 -> rc 0, scotch.dir has 230 objects, identical set to the patched tree (alt/TESTS.log). Not built, PTSCOTCH list and header files not converted.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Single source of truth, but hides the list from CMake users, parses a Makefile with regexes, and leaves headers/generated files hand-listed; IDE integration loses the list.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Not his style: the CMake files are maintained by hand by the Inria CMake contributors and nothing in the tree parses one build system from the other.

cleanup_done: Patch 0002 removes src/libscotch/common_error.c (never built by the Makefile, no reference anywhere else: git grep common_error -> only its CMake entry) and patch 0003 removes the standalone compilation of src/esmumps/symbol_fax.c; duplicate bgraph_cost.c entry removed.
test_added: ci/check_sources.sh (new, patch 0005): compares the Makefile object lists with the CMake source lists of libscotch, libptscotch, libesmumps, libscotchmetis and libptscotchparmetis; exits 1 on any difference. Not a src/check test (no natural home there: the defect is in the build description).
notes: CI job to add (G30, not done here): in ci/build_cmake.sh, before 'mkdir -p build': './ci/check_sources.sh || fatal'. The script is POSIX sh (sed/sort/diff), takes the src directory as optional argument.

our_title: Installed SCOTCHConfig.cmake includes EsMUMPS target files that suffixed builds never install
ran: Pristine suffixed install: cmake -S src-base -B cm/suffix32 -DSCOTCH_NAME_SUFFIX=_pys -DENABLE_TESTS=OFF ... && make install; consumer: cmake -S repro/BLD-02/consumer -B b -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=cm/inst-suffix32 -> 'CMake Error at .../SCOTCHConfig.cmake:111 (include): include could not find requested file: .../esmumpsTargets.cmake' and the same at :114 for ptesmumpsTargets.cmake, rc=1. Patched: configure prints '-- EsMUMPS library not built because SCOTCH_NAME_SUFFIX is set', SCOTCHConfig.cmake has if(OFF), consumer configures (SCOTCH_FOUND=1, SCOTCH_LIBESMUMPS_FOUND empty), builds and runs. Unsuffixed, no-esmumps and static patched installs: consumer OK. repro/BLD-02/README.
severity_note: Lower than the review's High: only installs configured with SCOTCH_NAME_SUFFIX are affected (CI never builds one, BLD-14), but for those every find_package(SCOTCH) is a hard error.
evidence: src/CMakeLists.txt:224 'if(BUILD_LIBESMUMPS AND NOT USE_SUFFIX)' / :225 'add_subdirectory(esmumps)'; cmake/SCOTCHConfig.cmake.in:85 'if(@BUILD_LIBESMUMPS@)' / :87 'include("${CMAKE_CURRENT_LIST_DIR}/esmumpsTargets.cmake")' / :90 'include("${CMAKE_CURRENT_LIST_DIR}/ptesmumpsTargets.cmake")'; CMakeLists.txt:99 'option(BUILD_LIBESMUMPS "Build EsMUMPS library" ON)' is never changed when USE_SUFFIX is set (:86-88).
upstream_change: none: file untouched between v7.0.16 and v7.0.17 (only CMakeLists.txt's version mark, 6ad2737, and ci/test_cmake.sh, ad24b21, changed)
review_accuracy: Accurate; its first fix ('@BUILD_LIBESMUMPS@ AND NOT @USE_SUFFIX@') would work but leaves BUILD_LIBESMUMPS lying about what is built, and USE_SUFFIX is unset (not OFF) without a suffix, which configure_package_config_file would substitute as an empty string: 'if(ON AND NOT )' is a syntax error. The OPTIONAL variant hides the problem and leaves SCOTCH_LIBESMUMPS_FOUND=ON (verified at runtime, alt b).
first_pass_critique: Correct status and the right idea (one effective value), but source-read only although cmake was available; its preferred patch adds a second variable (BUILD_LIBESMUMPS_EFFECTIVE) instead of fixing BUILD_LIBESMUMPS itself where USE_SUFFIX is decided, and its sketch sets the variable in src/ after the fact. Its remark that the review's fix 'applies to ptesmumps implicitly' is right.

fix_options.label: a: decide once in the top-level file
fix_options.summary: Right after option(BUILD_LIBESMUMPS), turn it OFF with a STATUS message when USE_SUFFIX is set; src/CMakeLists.txt then tests BUILD_LIBESMUMPS alone and the config template needs no change.
fix_options.tested: Suffixed patched build + install + consumer find_package OK; unsuffixed, BUILD_LIBESMUMPS=OFF and static installs OK (repro/BLD-02/README).
fix_options.tradeoffs: Shadows the cache option with a normal variable (standard CMake practice; the cache entry still shows ON in a GUI, the status message explains).
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Keeps the existing @BUILD_LIBESMUMPS@ substitution of the template and the deliberate 'not with suffix' rule (src/CMakeLists.txt:224); one decision point, like option handling elsewhere in CMakeLists.txt (lines 84-88 set USE_SUFFIX from the suffix in the same way).

fix_options.label: b: include(... OPTIONAL)
fix_options.summary: Make the two esmumps includes of the template tolerant of missing files.
fix_options.tested: Applied to a copy of the pristine suffixed install: consumer configures but reports SCOTCH_LIBESMUMPS_FOUND=ON (alt/TESTS.log, repro/BLD-02/README).
fix_options.tradeoffs: One line, but wrong information exported (LIBESMUMPS_FOUND=ON with no library) and typos in the install layout become silent.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: He fixes causes, not symptoms (see the 7.0.17 series: no 'ignore the error' fixes).

fix_options.label: c: separate effective variable
fix_options.summary: set(BUILD_LIBESMUMPS_EFFECTIVE ON/OFF) in src/CMakeLists.txt and substitute it in the template (first pass's option).
fix_options.tested: Configured suffixed: generated SCOTCHConfig.cmake has if(OFF) around the esmumps includes (alt/TESTS.log).
fix_options.tradeoffs: Works, but adds a second name for the same notion and leaves BUILD_LIBESMUMPS=ON meaning 'maybe'.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Acceptable but less tidy than (a); nothing in the tree uses *_EFFECTIVE variables.

test_added: ; no src/check home; a CI matrix entry with SCOTCH_NAME_SUFFIX is BLD-14 (another group). Note that a suffixed CMake build with ENABLE_TESTS=ON does not even link (extra.json PS2-G29-4).

our_title: Both MeTiS libraries carry the metis.h generation rule; parallel make runs dummysizes twice on it
ran: Pristine: grep -l 'Generating metis.h' cm/base32/src/libscotchmetis/CMakeFiles/*/build.make -> scotchmetisv3.dir, metis_h.dir, scotchmetisv5.dir; Makefile2: neither library depends on metis_h. Race: 10 x (rm src/include/metis.h; make -j8 all | grep -c 'Generating metis.h') -> 2 in 9 runs, 1 once (repro/BLD-12/race-base-all.log). Patched: 10 x -> 1 (race-patched-all.log). Caveat: 'make -j8 scotchmetisv3 scotchmetisv5' shows 12 x 1 because CMake's top-level Makefile is .NOTPARALLEL for command-line goals; CI runs 'make -j16' (all).
severity_note: As the review: nondeterministic parallel build in CI (make -j16); two dummysizes processes rewrite the same header while the other library may be compiling against it. No corrupted header observed in 10 runs, but nothing prevents it.
evidence: src/libscotchmetis/CMakeLists.txt:89 '    ${GENERATED_INCLUDE_DIR}/metis.h' inside add_library(scotchmetisv${version} ...) for version in 3 5; :111 '  add_dependencies(scotchmetisv${version} scotch_h metisf_h)' (metis_h missing); :193 '    add_dependencies(ptscotchparmetisv${version} ptscotch_h)' (parmetis_h missing, single consumer so no race).
upstream_change: none: file untouched between v7.0.16 and v7.0.17 (only CMakeLists.txt's version mark, 6ad2737, and ci/test_cmake.sh, ad24b21, changed)
review_accuracy: Accurate; the Makefile-generator mechanism is exactly what the generated build.make files show. Its fix line mentions parmetis_h, which is only a consistency fix (one consumer), and 'drop the generated header from per-target sources', which is optional once the dependency exists.
first_pass_critique: Right status and preferred option, and right that parmetis.h is not racy. Source-read although it could have run the Makefile generator; its note that option 2 'needs GENERATED set' is moot (the property is already set at :53). Missed the .NOTPARALLEL trap, which makes a naive reproduction report 'no race'.

fix_options.label: a: depend on the generation targets
fix_options.summary: add_dependencies(scotchmetisv${version} scotch_h metis_h metisf_h) and add parmetis_h to the ParMeTiS library for consistency.
fix_options.tested: Patched: Makefile2 has scotchmetisv{3,5}.dir/all -> metis_h.dir/all; 10 x make -j8 all -> 'Generating metis.h' once each; ctest 181/181.
fix_options.tradeoffs: None; one extra ordering edge. The rule is still attached to the libraries' build.make but is never out of date when they run.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: metisf_h is already listed on the same line: metis_h was simply forgotten; adm2dgr already does add_dependencies(adm2dgr parmetis_h) (:227).

fix_options.label: b: drop the generated headers from the source lists
fix_options.summary: Remove metis.h/metisf.h (and parmetis.h) from add_library() and keep only the target dependencies.
fix_options.tested: Configured: the metis.h rule now appears only in metis_h.dir/build.make (alt/TESTS.log). Not built.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Removes the duplicate rule entirely, but headers vanish from the targets' file lists (IDE/PUBLIC_HEADER remain through set_target_properties), diverging from how scotch.h is listed everywhere else.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: He lists generated headers as sources in every library (scotch.h in SCOTCH_C_SOURCES, ptscotch.h, esmumps.h); (b) breaks that pattern for one directory.

fix_options.label: c: one ALL target for both headers
fix_options.summary: add_custom_target(metis_headers ALL DEPENDS metis.h metisf.h) and depend on it.
fix_options.tested: Configured: Makefile2 shows both libraries depending on metis_headers.dir/all (alt/TESTS.log).
fix_options.tradeoffs: A third target for what metis_h/metisf_h already provide.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Redundant with the existing per-header targets; not his minimal style.

our_title: cmake_minimum_required(3.10) while NAME_WLE, LibLZMA::LibLZMA (3.14) and cmake -E cat (3.18) are used
ran: Facts from the cmake 4.4.4 built-in docs: 'cmake --help-command get_filename_component' -> 'versionadded:: 3.14 Added the LAST_EXT and NAME_WLE modes'; '--help-module FindLibLZMA' -> 'LibLZMA::LibLZMA versionadded:: 3.14'; FindBZip2 -> BZip2::BZip2 3.12; FindZLIB -> 3.1; FindThreads -> 3.1; FindMPI -> 3.10; FIXTURES_SETUP -> 3.7; if(GREATER_EQUAL) -> 3.7. Patched tree: full configure/build/ctest with the new minimum, 32-bit and INTSIZE=64: no policy warning, 181/181 tests. Alternative b (floor 3.14 with replacements) built and its graph_dump2 test passes (repro/BLD-13/README).
read_only: No CMake between 3.10 and 3.17 exists on this host (no network), so the failure on those versions was not observed; 'cmake -E cat' being 3.18 is from memory (the 4.4.4 manual carries no versionadded note for it) and matches the review.
severity_note: Lower than the review's Medium: an old CMake fails at configure time with a clear error (unknown NAME_WLE / LibLZMA::LibLZMA target), so nothing wrong is built; the cost is a false promise in README.md, h_c.tex and the top-level file.
evidence: CMakeLists.txt:44 'cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.10)'; README.md:70 '* With CMake, using version 3.10 or higher:'; doc/src/handson/h_c.tex:19 '  possibly CMake, version at least~3.10;'; src/check/CMakeLists.txt:69 '  get_filename_component(file_we ${src} NAME_WLE)'; :289 '  COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -E cat ...'; src/libscotch/CMakeLists.txt:570 '  target_link_libraries(scotch PRIVATE LibLZMA::LibLZMA)'; ci/test_cmake.sh:10 'ctest ... --output-junit' (3.21, so the maintainers' CI runners have >= 3.21).
upstream_change: ad24b21 'Enable test output on failure for CMake in CI' touches ci/test_cmake.sh only (unrelated)
review_accuracy: Accurate; it misses LibLZMA::LibLZMA (3.14) and BZip2::BZip2 (3.12), which bind the library build itself (not only the tests) to >= 3.14, and the doc/src/handson/h_c.tex mention.
first_pass_critique: Right, and it did spot LibLZMA::LibLZMA; it missed BZip2::BZip2 (3.12) and the hands-on doc. Its option 3 sketch for '-E cat' was never written; a working one is alt b here (cmake -P script, since shell 'cat' is not portable to NMake).

fix_options.label: a: require 3.18 and say so
fix_options.summary: cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.18); README.md and doc/src/handson/h_c.tex updated.
fix_options.tested: Patched 32/64-bit CMake builds and ctest 181/181 under the new policy floor (CMP0074..CMP0104 NEW); no warning.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Drops CMake 3.10-3.17 hosts (Ubuntu 18.04/20.04, Debian 10); CI runners already need 3.21 for --output-junit. The PDF/PS docs are not regenerated here (the maintainer rebuilds them from the .tex).
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Truthful and one line; the CMake maintainers (Fuentes/Pruvost/Barthelemy) added NAME_WLE and -E cat without thinking about 3.10, and his CI uses 3.21 features. The version-mark commit 6ad2737 shows he edits CMakeLists.txt and docs together.

fix_options.label: b: keep a 3.14 floor, replace the 3.18 construct
fix_options.summary: NAME_WLE -> NAME + string(REGEX REPLACE); 'cmake -E cat' -> a cmake -P script cmake/Modules/ConcatFiles.cmake; declare 3.14 (needed by LibLZMA::LibLZMA anyway).
fix_options.tested: Built test_scotch_graph_dump2 and test_scotch_mesh_build_f on a patched copy: graph_dump2 test passes, generated file byte-identical to cat, .f90 generated (repro/BLD-13/README).
fix_options.tradeoffs: Keeps 3.14-3.17 hosts, at the price of a new module file and a regex for what CMake does natively; touches src/check/CMakeLists.txt (G30's file).
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Possible, but he has no CI on old CMake to keep the promise; more code to carry for hosts that are end-of-life.

fix_options.label: c: 3.14 for the library, 3.18 only when ENABLE_TESTS
fix_options.summary: Fatal error when ENABLE_TESTS is ON with CMake < 3.18; floor 3.14.
fix_options.tested: Configured OK with 4.4.4 (alt/TESTS.log); the < 3.18 branch not exercised (no such CMake).
fix_options.tradeoffs: Honest split, but two floors to document; ENABLE_TESTS defaults to ON so most users hit 3.18 anyway.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Unnecessarily subtle for the gain.

notes: Assumption stated: 'cmake -E cat' introduced in 3.18 (CMake 3.18 release notes), not verifiable from the installed cmake.

our_title: COMMON_RANDOM_FIXED_SEED, SCOTCH_DETERMINISTIC and FreeBSD macros exported in scotchTargets.cmake
ran: Pristine install: grep INTERFACE_COMPILE_DEFINITIONS cm/inst-base32/lib/cmake/scotch/scotchTargets.cmake -> 'INTERFACE_COMPILE_DEFINITIONS "COMMON_RANDOM_FIXED_SEED"'; consumer program prints 'COMMON_RANDOM_FIXED_SEED leaked into consumer'. Patched install: no INTERFACE_COMPILE_DEFINITIONS line; consumer prints 'no scotch-internal macros in consumer' (shared, static and suffixed installs); in-tree flags.make of test_common_random and gmap still contain -DCOMMON_RANDOM_FIXED_SEED; ctest 181/181. Alt b (PRIVATE only) demonstrated wrong: test_common_random compiled without the macro against the fixed-seed library -> 'ERROR: main: two consecutive runs yield same values.' rc=1 (repro/BLD-24/README).
read_only: FreeBSD branch (cpu_set_t=cpuset_t, __BSD_VISIBLE) not executed: no FreeBSD host; in-tree users found by grep (test_scotch_context.c:205,330,361; common_thread.h:84 via common.h).
severity_note: As the review: silent and mostly harmless on Linux (one -D in user builds), a type-renaming macro in user code on FreeBSD.
evidence: src/libscotch/CMakeLists.txt:542 '  target_compile_definitions(scotch PUBLIC cpu_set_t=cpuset_t __BSD_VISIBLE)'; :546 '  target_compile_definitions(scotch PUBLIC COMMON_RANDOM_FIXED_SEED)'; :547 '  target_compile_definitions(scotch PUBLIC SCOTCH_DETERMINISTIC)'; :550 same as :546; by contrast :559/:564/:569/:575 use PRIVATE for the compression and thread macros.
upstream_change: none: file untouched between v7.0.16 and v7.0.17 (only CMakeLists.txt's version mark, 6ad2737, and ci/test_cmake.sh, ad24b21, changed)
review_accuracy: Accurate on the leak; its fix 'make them PRIVATE' breaks the in-tree test_common_random (shown at runtime) and, on FreeBSD, every in-tree program that includes common.h (cpu_set_t field in common_thread.h).
first_pass_critique: Right on all points, including the BUILD_INTERFACE need; source-read only. Nothing to add except the runtime proof of why PRIVATE is wrong.

fix_options.label: a: PUBLIC $<BUILD_INTERFACE:...>
fix_options.summary: Wrap each definition in $<BUILD_INTERFACE:>: build-tree targets keep it, export() strips it.
fix_options.tested: See 'ran': export has no definitions, in-tree flags unchanged, consumer clean, ctest 181/181 (32 and 64-bit).
fix_options.tradeoffs: Projects that add_subdirectory() Scotch still see the macros (as before); only installed packages change. ptscotch inherits through its PUBLIC link to scotch, as before.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: The same file already uses $<BUILD_INTERFACE:> / $<INSTALL_INTERFACE:> for include directories (:531-535); three-line change.

fix_options.label: b: PRIVATE
fix_options.summary: The review's fix.
fix_options.tested: Shown to break test_common_random (repro/BLD-24/README); not built as a tree.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Breaks in-tree tests and FreeBSD in-tree programs.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Would be reverted after the first CI run.

fix_options.label: c: scotch_internal INTERFACE target
fix_options.summary: Carry the definitions on a non-exported INTERFACE library linked PRIVATE by scotch and by the tests.
fix_options.tested: Configured: test_common_random flags.make still has -DCOMMON_RANDOM_FIXED_SEED (alt/TESTS.log); not built; src/scotch tools and esmumps/metis not converted in the diff.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Cleanest separation but touches every consumer in the tree (tools, esmumps, metis, check) and src/check/CMakeLists.txt (G30).
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Too much churn for three macros; nothing similar in the tree.

notes: SCOTCH_METIS_VERSION and SCOTCH_PTSCOTCH stay PUBLIC on the MeTiS targets on purpose: library_metis.h:211-223 selects prototypes with them.

our_title: Stray brace in the FreeBSD host test and 'integer size' message in the IDXSIZE branch

fix_options.summary: if(CMAKE_HOST_SYSTEM_NAME MATCHES "FreeBSD") and 'Invalid index size value'.
fix_options.tested: probe + configure (see 'ran').
fix_options.tradeoffs: None.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Trivial; same if(VAR MATCHES) idiom as the BLD-06 fix in the same file.

fix_options.summary: if(CMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME STREQUAL "FreeBSD") (the macros affect compiled code, so the target matters when cross-compiling).

our_title: Open MPI regex needs spaces around 'Open MPI', so --oversubscribe is never added to MPIEXEC_PREFLAGS
ran: repro/BLD-06/mpiver: find_package(MPI) with MPI_DETERMINE_LIBRARY_VERSION + the 7.0.17 lines verbatim: 'MPI_C_LIBRARY_VERSION_STRING=[Open MPI v5.0.7, package: Debian OpenMPI, ...]', '7.0.17: Open MPI NOT detected (found_suite=[])', 'fixed: Found OpenMPI'. severity_note: Lower than the review's Medium: test-only (MPI tests fail on hosts with fewer cores than ranks); the libraries are unaffected.

our_title: Unquoted, possibly empty operands around the MPI vendor regex; empty version string is a fatal error
ran: cmake -DOMPI_STRING="MPICH 4.1" -P repro/BLD-06/probe.cmake -> found_suite=[] and the unquoted if(NOT ${found_suite} STREQUAL "") still evaluates (CMake tolerates it); cmake -DOMPI_STRING="" -P probe.cmake -> 'CMake Error at probe.cmake:3 (string): string sub-command REGEX, mode MATCHALL needs at least 5 arguments total to command.' Patched form: no error in either case.
severity_note: Raised from info: with an empty MPI_C_LIBRARY_VERSION_STRING (cross-compilation, try_run disabled) the 7.0.17 code aborts configuration; the empty if() operand itself is tolerated by CMake.
evidence: src/CMakeLists.txt:181 '... found_suite ${MPI_C_LIBRARY_VERSION_STRING})' (unquoted argument vanishes when empty); :182 '    if(NOT ${found_suite} STREQUAL "")'.
upstream_change: none: file untouched between v7.0.16 and v7.0.17 (only CMakeLists.txt's version mark, 6ad2737, and ci/test_cmake.sh, ad24b21, changed)
first_pass_critique: Right lead, wrong emphasis: the if() with an empty operand is harmless in practice, the string(REGEX) with a vanished argument is the real failure.
